subject: Coffee & Tea
title: The Legend of Shen Nung
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Legend of Shen Nung.

hook.text: In 2737 BC, Chinese Emperor Shen Nung sat beneath a tree as leaves blew into his boiling water.

buildup.text: He drank the infusion and felt refreshed and alert. The leaves came from a wild Camellia sinensis tree.

discovery.text: This legend, likely mythical, places tea's origin nearly 5,000 years ago in southern China.

twist.text: Archaeological evidence confirms tea drinking in China by at least 2100 BC—the legend isn't far off.

climax.text: What began as an accidental brew became the world's most consumed beverage after water.

punchline.text: A leaf fell into hot water. Five millennia followed.

quiz.question: Which plant produces all true tea?

details.summary: Chinese mythology credits Emperor Shen Nung with discovering tea around 2737 BCE when leaves from a wild tea tree blew into his pot of boiling water. He tasted the infusion and found it refreshing. While almost certainly a myth, the story places tea's origin at the very dawn of Chinese civilization.
details.whyItMatters: The Shen Nung legend reveals how deeply tea is embedded in Chinese cultural identity. Like Kaldi for coffee, this origin myth anchors tea in a specific civilization.
takeaways: Legend places tea's discovery at 2737 BCE by Emperor Shen Nung
Leaves allegedly blew into his boiling water by accident
The myth connects tea to the origins of Chinese civilization

faq.question: Is the Shen Nung story historically true?
faq.answer: Almost certainly not. Shen Nung is a legendary figure, not a confirmed historical emperor. The story first appeared in writing centuries after the supposed event. It serves as a cultural origin narrative rather than historical fact, placing tea at the heart of Chinese identity.

faq.question: When was tea actually first consumed by humans?
faq.answer: Archaeological evidence suggests tea was consumed in China at least 2,000 years ago. Physical tea remains have been found in tombs from the Han dynasty. The true origins are probably even older, but predate written records.
